Malignant smooth-muscle soft-tissue neoplasm; organ-specific sites vary. EBV association is not universal; no additional organ qualifies across the umbrella.
Oocyte and early embryonic developmental failure causing female infertility; purely reproductive, without demonstrated endocrine dysfunction.
Carcinoma arising in the hypopharynx; pharyngeal structures belong to the pulmonary axis.
Inherited ichthyosis; the concept explicitly excludes CNS and eye involvement. No established metabolic disorder is specified.

IRF7-related primary immunodeficiency; severe influenza susceptibility does not establish common intrinsic pulmonary damage.
Small-vessel disease defines retinal and cerebral injury; nephropathy/glomerulosclerosis 30-79%. Hepatic lesions and anemia also 30-79%, omitted by cap.
Structural aneurysmal dilatation of coronary vessels; an inflammatory cause is not universal.
Poliosis, ASD and skeletal malformations define syndrome; respiratory anomalies 80-99%, with bronchomalacia reported. Myopia/strabismus 30-79% omitted by cap.
Dystroglycan glycosylation disorder with myopathy; developmental/intellectual impairment occurs in >30% across POMT1 forms. Eye anomalies chiefly affect severe subtypes.
Early neurodegeneration and microcytic hypochromic anemia define the syndrome; both documented in the reported patient.
Congenital structural defect of the ocular lens.
Congenital ocular motility disorder; callosal hypoplasia 6/7, developmental delay 4/7 and axonal neuropathy 4/8 support common neurologic involvement.
Syndromic intellectual disability with developmental delay 12/12 and seizures 5/6; isolated skeletal and ocular findings do not establish common damage.
FGF23 excess causes hypophosphatemia and osteomalacia; hormonal phosphate wasting does not establish kidney injury. Nephrocalcinosis may reflect treatment.
Peroxisome biogenesis disorder; cataracts 2/2, intellectual disability/neuropathy and progressive hearing loss reported in 1/1 assessed; very small series.
Congenital submucosal defect of the shared laryngotracheal-esophageal partition; both airway and esophageal anatomy are defining.
Defining gastrointestinal hamartomatous polyposis; anemia is secondary to intestinal blood loss, without direct blood-organ disease. Cancers are separate diagnoses.
Scarring causes outward turning of the eyelid; localized ocular disease.
Neoplasm of uterine supporting ligaments, a reproductive site; these ligaments are outside the locomotor musculoskeletal axis.
Degenerative disease of the peripheral cornea.
Defining intestinal aganglionosis, distal phalangeal hypoplasia and absent/hypoplastic nails; all three are core syndrome features.
Corticosteroid-induced skeletal muscle disease; treatment is the cause of this explicitly defined myopathy.
Primary ischemic necrosis of bone; impaired bone perfusion does not establish an independent vascular disorder.
